zh: 第三，通常你们的定价会高于市场上其他定价比你们低得多的玩家。

en: So if you can be the number one or two seller there, you come into a system like Rant, that is where the magic is going to happen.
zh: 所以如果你能在那里成为第一或第二的销售，再进入像 Rant 这样的系统，那就是奇迹将要发生的地方。

en: If you were to name a company.
zh: 如果让你点出一家公司。

en: I can't give away the secret sauce.
zh: 我不能透露秘诀。

en: I'll name one.
zh: 我来点一家。

en: I'll name one.
zh: 我来点一家。

en: Six cents.
zh: Six cents。

en: Because they have a low MPS.

en: Products maybe not great.
zh: 产品也许不算好。

speaker: Unknown
en: Correct.
zh: 没错。

en: But close good customers.
zh: 但是拿下优质客户。

speaker: Unknown
en: Exactly.
zh: 完全正确。

en: In fact, just yesterday, one of our top enterprise sellers sent me a email from a customer.

en: That said this huge review that they sent internally, they want to offer a case study.

en: And we didn't even prompt them at all.
zh: 而我们甚至完全没有主动要求过。

en: And Alex had said, I've never seen this in my 15 years of sales.

en: You've just been selling shit products.

speaker: Unknown
en: When you're trying to determine greatness in a candidate in terms of where they've come from before, how do you unpick whether it was truly them or whether they were just an order taker?
zh: 当你试图判断一个候选人的优秀程度、看他们之前来自哪里时，你如何分辨那真的是他们自己的功劳，还是他们只是一个接单员？

speaker: Unknown
en: You can have two different situations.
zh: 你可能会遇到两种不同的情况。

speaker: Unknown
en: One, they're just an order taker, which isn't very difficult.
zh: 一，他们只是一个接单员，这并不难。

speaker: Unknown
en: Or two, they're at Twilio and they sign up Uber and they sign Uber when it starts and then it expands into what it becomes and they get the credit for that.
zh: 或者二，他们在 Twilio,他们签下了 Uber,在 Uber 刚起步时签下，然后随着它发展壮大而扩张，并因此获得功劳。

speaker: Unknown
en: How do you determine true quality versus happenstance or order taking?
zh: 你如何判断真正的实力 versus 偶然运气或接单？

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, you have to decompose their number.
zh: 嗯，你必须分解他们的数字。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so, okay, you did 2 million.
zh: 所以，好吧，你做了 200 万。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's great.
zh: 那很好。

speaker: Unknown
en: How much of it was inbound?
zh: 其中多少是入站(Inbound)?

speaker: Unknown
en: How much of it was outbound?
zh: 多少是出站(Outbound)?

speaker: Unknown
en: How much of it was expansion?
zh: 多少是扩张(Expansion)?

speaker: Unknown
en: How much of it was sourced by your founder?
zh: 多少是你的创始人带来的？

speaker: Unknown
en: How much of it was from existing opportunities that you inherited?
zh: 多少来自你接手时的既有商机？

speaker: Unknown
en: And then you really have to drill down such that you can spot and figure out if someone is
zh: 然后你必须真正深入挖掘，这样才能发现并搞清楚一个人是否

speaker: Unknown
en: Bullshitting you.
zh: 在忽悠你。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then to get even more deep into testing their acumen around sales, it's, all right, talk to me about two deals.
zh: 然后要更深入地测试他们的销售敏锐度，就是：好吧，跟我讲两个交易。

speaker: Unknown
en: You have to make them reconstruct them chronologically.
zh: 你必须让他们按时间顺序重构这些交易。

speaker: Unknown
en: The best candidates give so much texture and like you're really trying to figure out, well, how did you advance this?
zh: 最好的候选人会给出大量细节，你其实是在试图搞清楚：那么，你是如何推进这笔交易的？

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, what was it?
zh: 那么，具体是什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: Were you articulating business value?
zh: 你是否在阐述商业价值？

speaker: Unknown
en: Was it some workflow that you tied to a business outcome?
zh: 是否有某个你绑定到业务成果的工作流？

speaker: Unknown
en: They'll know that.
zh: 他们会知道这些。

speaker: Unknown
en: And if they can't describe that, not a good sign.
zh: 如果他们描述不出来，那不是个好兆头。

speaker: Unknown
en: The inverse is also true.
zh: 反过来也成立。

speaker: Unknown
en: You want to understand, talk to me about a deal that keeps you up at night.
zh: 你要了解，跟我讲一个让你夜不能寐的交易。

speaker: Unknown
en: Why did you lose it?
zh: 你为什么输了它？

speaker: Unknown
en: If they can't unpack why they've lost an opportunity, was it they were single-threaded?
zh: 如果他们无法剖析为什么丢掉一个机会——是他们单线联系(single-threaded)吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: They didn't build a champion.
zh: 他们没有培养出内部拥护者(champion)。

speaker: Unknown
en: There was no business value.
zh: 没有商业价值。

speaker: Unknown
en: The product wasn't good enough.
zh: 产品不够好。

speaker: Unknown
en: They didn't qualify well enough.

en: Figuring that out and testing for it is actually incredibly important in an interview process.

speaker: Unknown
en: What if I said to you, hey, I get you, one of the decision makers is friends with a competitor, and that's why.
zh: 如果我对你说,嘿,我理解你,其中一个决策者是竞争对手的朋友,这就是原因。

speaker: Unknown
en: I kind of hate it, but I also get it.
zh: 我有点讨厌这个,但我也能理解。

speaker: Unknown
en: But blame deflection can also be genuine.
zh: 但甩锅也可能是真的。

speaker: Unknown
en: How do you determine good versus bad on that sort of order?
zh: 你如何判断这类情况的好坏?

speaker: Unknown
en: Totally.
zh: 完全可以。

speaker: Unknown
en: But you should be able to suss that out early enough in the cycle and you should confront it head on.
zh: 但你应该能够在流程早期就把这个摸清楚,而且你应该正面直面它。

en: Hey, Harry, I know you're evaluating us and another competitor.
zh: 嘿,Harry,我知道你正在评估我们和另一个竞争对手。

en: I see you have a shared board member with that competitor.
zh: 我看到你和那个竞争对手有一位共同的董事会成员。

speaker: Unknown
en: Is that going to get in the way of this decision?
zh: 这会妨碍这次决策吗?

speaker: Unknown
en: Like, how are you actually evaluating it?
zh: 就是说,你实际上是怎么评估的?

speaker: Unknown
en: Is it on its merits or is it not?
zh: 是基于产品本身的优势,还是不是?

speaker: Unknown
en: A seller should be able to articulate and communicate that to me.
zh: 一个销售应该能够向我清晰地表达和沟通这些。

speaker: Unknown
en: They shouldn't find out about that at the final second after they've rallied all of these internal resources to take a deal through a cycle.
zh: 他们不应该在最后一刻,也就是在调动了所有内部资源把一笔交易推进了整个流程之后,才发现这件事。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I've done pretty well in this set of questions.
zh: 所以我在这套问题上表现得相当不错。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm running through this hypothetical interview process with you.

en: Next step, do I need to do a demo?
zh: 下一步,我需要做演示吗?

en: Do I need to do some form of case study with you?

en: So you definitely have to do what we call a business case.
zh: 所以你肯定要做我们所说的商业案例(business case)。

en: Which is assuming the role of a seller at RAMP and you have to go through a discovery call.
zh: 也就是假设你是 RAMP 的一名销售,你必须完成一次探索性电话(discovery call)。

speaker: Unknown
en: We'll give a prompt in advance and we really test for three things.
zh: 我们会提前给出一个题目,我们真正测试三样东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: Those three things are RAMP as a business and as a product.
zh: 这三样东西是:RAMP 作为一家公司和作为一个产品。

speaker: Unknown
en: Two, the prospective company in question.
zh: 二,所讨论的潜在客户公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like, are you doing your research?
zh: 就是说,你有没有做功课?

speaker: Unknown
en: Do you know what's going on?
zh: 你了解他们的动向吗?

speaker: Unknown
en: Have you read their 10K?
zh: 你读过他们的 10K 报告吗?

speaker: Unknown
en: Things of that sort.
zh: 诸如此类的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then the third is just selling fundamentals.
zh: 然后第三是销售基本功。

speaker: Unknown
en: Do they have executive presence?
zh: 他们有没有高管气场?

speaker: Unknown
en: Can they get second and third level discovery questions?
zh: 他们能不能问到第二层、第三层的探索性问题?

speaker: Unknown
en: Can they quantify pain?
zh: 他们能不能量化痛点?

speaker: Unknown
en: Can they articulate the value?
zh: 他们能不能清晰表达价值?

speaker: Unknown
en: And then more than anything, not to oversimplify, would I buy a product from this person?
zh: 然后最重要的是,不想过度简化地说,我会从这个人手里买产品吗?

speaker: Unknown
en: If I can't say that with conviction, I'm not going to hire them.
zh: 如果我不能带着确信这么说,我就不会雇他。

speaker: Unknown
en: I feel the same way about hiring leaders.
zh: 我对招聘领导者也是同样的看法。

speaker: Unknown
en: If I'm trying to hire a leader and I don't think I would work for that person, I wouldn't make the call.
zh: 如果我要招一位领导者,而我不认为自己会为那个人工作,我就不会做这个决定。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so you sit down with me and you realize that you would buy from me and you do want to work with me.
zh: 那么你和我坐下来,你意识到你会从我这里买东西,而且你确实想和我一起工作。

en: What does the offer stage look like?
zh: 那么 offer 阶段是什么样的?

speaker: Unknown
en: What do you look for in how I respond to equity versus title versus comp?
zh: 在我如何回应股权、头衔和薪酬之间做权衡时,你看重什么?

speaker: Unknown
en: I have so many thoughts on this.
zh: 我对此有非常多的想法。

speaker: Unknown
en: It so depends on where you are in your career.
zh: 这很大程度上取决于你在职业生涯的哪个阶段。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you're a seller looking to join an early stage company, thinking about equity, cash, and comp is actually the wrong thing to index on.
zh: 如果你是一个想加入早期公司的销售,把股权、现金和薪酬作为核心考量指标其实是错误的做法。

zh: 正确的核心考量指标是市场、人才密度、业务,以及创始人。

en: Why the market?
zh: 为什么是市场?

en: Because there's structural advantages if you pick a business that can continue to find growth vectors.
zh: 因为如果你选了一项能够持续找到增长向量的业务,那就有结构性优势。

zh: 销售在拆解开来之后,很大程度上是一个工程问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so you need to build the systems to help give you leverage and automate such that you can create a ton of capacity.
zh: 所以你需要构建系统来给你杠杆并实现自动化,从而让你创造出大量的产能。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I give a lot of credit to Kareem early on with providing engineering resources to myself to build out our OATS program super early on in the business.
zh: 我非常感谢 Kareem 早期为我自己提供工程资源,在公司非常早期就搭建了我们的 OATS 项目。

en: I'm so sorry.
zh: 非常抱歉。

en: What is an OATS program?
zh: 什么是 OATS 项目?

en: Why is it a data infrastructure problem?
zh: 为什么它是一个数据基础设施问题?

speaker: Unknown
en: Why is it a maths problem?
zh: 为什么它是一个数学问题?

speaker: Unknown
en: Can you just help me understand this?
zh: 你能帮我理解一下吗?

speaker: Unknown
en: Seriously?
zh: 是认真的吗?

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, so outbound used to primarily be a writing and a calling problem.
zh: 是的,外呼销售(outbound)过去主要是一个写作和打电话的问题。

en: I think increasingly it's becoming an engineering problem.
zh: 我觉得它正越来越多地变成一个工程问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: In late 2020, early 21, even before the rise of AI, we built our own internal infrastructure to help automate a lot of our outbound.
zh: 在 2020 年底、2021 年初,甚至在 AI 崛起之前,我们就构建了自己的内部基础设施,来帮助自动化我们大量的外呼工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that's what OATS is an acronym for, Outbound Automation Team.
zh: 这就是 OATS 这个缩写的由来,Outbound Automation Team(外呼自动化团队)。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so let me break this down.
zh: 让我拆解一下。

speaker: Unknown
en: So the team was understanding what I was doing to go to market, how I was creating signals inside of accounts.
zh: 团队在理解我是如何进入市场的,我是如何在客户账户内部创建信号的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the signals could be unbounded.
zh: 而这些信号可以是无边界的。

speaker: Unknown
en: It could be a new hire, just join the business.
zh: 可能是有一个新员工刚加入这家公司。

zh: 可能是我和这个人上的是同一所大学。

zh: 我们的股权表上有重叠的投资人。

en: And that was very manual.
zh: 而这过去是非常手工的。

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, you got to build the templates, you got to find the contact data.
zh: 你知道,你得搭建模板,你得找联系人数据。

speaker: Unknown
en: Why is our sales team doing that?
zh: 为什么要让我们的销售团队做这些?

speaker: Unknown
en: They should be focused on just speaking with the customer and helping solve their business problems and getting ramp deployed.
zh: 他们应该专注于和客户交谈、帮助解决他们的业务问题、把 ramp 部署上线。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so our team of engineers built a lot of automation to do the list scraping, do the email outreach, and it was...
zh: 所以我们的工程师团队构建了大量自动化来做名单抓取、做邮件外呼,然后……

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm so sorry.
zh: 非常抱歉。

speaker: Unknown
en: If I'm a founder then listening to this wanting to do the same, what do I do?
zh: 如果我是一个创始人,听到这里也想做同样的事,我该怎么做?

speaker: Unknown
en: I tell my engineers to get Zoom info?
zh: 我让我的工程师去买 Zoom Info 吗?

speaker: Unknown
en: No, that's part of it.
zh: 不,那只是其中一部分。

speaker: Unknown
en: You tell one or two of your top engineers that, hey, we could build the coolest product in the world.
zh: 你要告诉你最顶尖的一两个工程师:嘿,我们可以做出世界上最酷的产品。

speaker: Unknown
en: It doesn't fucking matter if it doesn't get into the hands of paying customers.
zh: 但如果它到不了付费客户的手里,那他妈的毫无意义。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so we need to obsess over growth as it's existential for our business.
zh: 所以我们需要痴迷于增长,因为这关乎我们公司的存亡。

speaker: Unknown
en: What are we solving for here?
zh: 我们在这里要解决的是什么?

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't get it.
zh: 我不明白。

speaker: Unknown
en: Are we solving for finding new leads or for outreach to them?
zh: 我们是要解决寻找新线索,还是对他们进行外呼?

speaker: Unknown
en: How do we handle the integrations of whether it should be an email or a LinkedIn message?
zh: 我们如何处理集成问题,比如该用邮件还是 LinkedIn 消息?

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, you're solving for coverage, right?
zh: 是的,你要解决的是覆盖率(coverage),对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: In the early innings of your business, you're not going to have an army of go-to-market talent.
zh: 在你业务的早期阶段,你不会有大批的 go-to-market 人才。

speaker: Unknown
en: You might have three to a half a dozen of folks that are responsible for outbounding.
zh: 你可能只有三到六个人负责外呼。

speaker: Unknown
en: Guess what?
zh: 你猜怎么着?

speaker: Unknown
en: If you do that manually, like maybe you could get a couple hundred emails out.
zh: 如果你手工做这件事,也许你能发出几百封邮件。

speaker: Unknown
en: Maybe you could make a hundred dials.
zh: 也许你能打一百个电话。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's not enough, especially in markets today where the TAMs are becoming more and more unbounded.
zh: 那是不够的,尤其是在今天这个 TAM 越来越无边界的市场里。

speaker: Unknown
en: You need leverage.
zh: 你需要杠杆。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so the problem you're solving for is coverage and brand awareness and getting your name out.
zh: 所以你要解决的问题是覆盖面、品牌知名度，以及让你的名字被外界知道。

speaker: Unknown
en: You just can't be dependent on sellers to do that.
zh: 你就是不能依赖销售人员来做这件事。

speaker: Unknown
en: Do you not think you have efficacy reduction, in other words, less efficient outbound with scale versus if I sent 20 really, really great messages that are researched, thoughtful, included a joke about our alma mater and a picture of me and my mum walking on the weekend, my efficiency would be through the roof.
zh: 你不认为存在效力递减吗，换句话说，规模化之后的外呼效率会变低，相比如果我只发 20 条真正非常好的、经过调研的、深思熟虑的消息，里面带一个关于我们母校的玩笑，还有一张我和我妈妈周末散步的照片，我的效率会高得离谱。

speaker: Unknown
en: A genuine asking, not telling.
zh: 是真诚地询问，而不是灌输。

speaker: Unknown
en: That is a concern.
zh: 这确实是一个担忧。

speaker: Unknown
en: You have to make the system recursive to actually understand what is yielding results such that it optimizes over time.
zh: 你必须让这个系统变成递归的，真正理解什么在产生成果，从而随时间不断优化。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so if you're just relying on automated emails that are going out and out now, that's irrelevant.
zh: 所以如果你只是依赖不断自动发出的邮件，那是无关紧要的。

speaker: Unknown
en: You have to constantly be A-B testing and pulling in what's actually going to yield the best results.
zh: 你必须持续做 A/B 测试，并纳入真正能带来最好结果的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then guess what?
zh: 然后猜怎么着？

speaker: Unknown
en: You still allow for manual outreach from your sales team.
zh: 你仍然允许你的销售团队进行人工外呼。

speaker: Unknown
en: Because they, to your point, if you're going to send 20 unbelievably curated notes, the likelihood of those getting responded, sure, it is higher.
zh: 因为，正如你所说，如果你要发 20 条精心打磨到不可思议的消息，它们得到回复的可能性，当然，是更高的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then the system can identify that, take that feedback, pull it in and start actually doing it at scale.
zh: 然后系统可以识别出这一点，接收那个反馈，把它纳入进来，并真正开始规模化地这样做。

speaker: Unknown
en: Do you have engineers in sales permanently?
zh: 你们有没有长期配置在销售里的工程师？

speaker: Unknown
en: This isn't like a one and done sales tool build.
zh: 这不是那种一次性建完就完事的销售工具。

speaker: Unknown
en: We have a growth engineering team.
zh: 我们有一个增长工程团队。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, I think there's at least half a dozen engineers that truly obsess over building products for go to market.
zh: 是的，我认为至少有六名工程师真正痴迷于为 go to market 打造产品。

speaker: Unknown
en: What's a good response rate when you're sending outbound in a tool like this?
zh: 当你用这样的工具发送外呼时，什么样的回复率算好的？

speaker: Unknown
en: Response rates over time since the acceleration of AI have actually regressed pretty meaningfully, but response rate isn't the right metric to index on.
zh: 自 AI 加速以来，回复率随着时间实际上已经显著倒退了，但回复率并不是应该看的核心指标。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's meeting response rate.
zh: 应该看的是会议回复率。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's like you can get a 5% response rate, but if they're saying, please never email me again or opt out or fuck off, that's not directionally helpful.
zh: 就是说，你可以得到 5% 的回复率，但如果他们说的是“请再也不要给我发邮件”或者退订或者“滚开”，那在方向上是没有帮助的。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's
zh: 它是

speaker: Unknown
en: And so it's how many convert to a meeting?
zh: 所以是有多少转化成了会议？

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that should be just a hair under 1%, I think, is a really, really strong standard.
zh: 我认为那应该略低于 1%，我觉得这是一个非常非常强的标准。

speaker: Unknown
en: So for every 100 emails you're sending, those convert to one.
zh: 也就是说你每发 100 封邮件，其中一封转化为会议。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's great.
zh: 那很不错。

speaker: Unknown
en: How quickly do you verticalize your sales team?
zh: 你们多快会把销售团队垂直化？

speaker: Unknown
en: Because all of this can become better, more efficient, more accurate with verticalization.
zh: 因为所有这些都可以通过垂直化变得更好、更高效、更精准。

speaker: Unknown
en: Hey, we've got clients including British Airways, Delta and Ryanair.
zh: 嘿，我们的客户包括英国航空、达美和瑞安航空。

speaker: Unknown
en: Oh, wow.
zh: 哦，哇。

speaker: Unknown
en: Okay.
zh: 好的。

speaker: Unknown
en: We're targeting the travel industry and specifically airlines.
zh: 我们瞄准的是旅游行业，具体来说是航空公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: Do you see what I mean?
zh: 你明白我的意思吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: When is the right time and how do you think about that?
zh: 什么时候是合适的时机，你是怎么考虑这件事的？

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think the right time to verticalize your business is when you need to pull the lever to inflect conversion.
zh: 我认为把业务垂直化的合适时机，是当你需要拉动这个杠杆来扭转转化率的时候。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think companies actually verticalize far too early, especially if you have a huge addressable market, you're in land grab market share mode.
zh: 我认为很多公司其实垂直化得太早了，尤其是当你有巨大的可触达市场、正处于抢占市场份额的模式时。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I think verticalizing the business may actually be counterproductive to doing that.
zh: 所以我认为垂直化业务实际上可能对做到这一点适得其反。

speaker: Unknown
en: But as you own more and more of the market, I think this is arbitrary, but I'd say, you know, three to 5%, guess what?
zh: 如果你能勾选这些框，都是肯定的，那就出手。

speaker: Unknown
en: The total amount of opportunities you can go after starts to become contained.
zh: 你可以去争取的机会总量开始变得有限了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so the lever that you need to pull is you need to be able to convert leads to close one at a higher clip.
zh: 所以你需要拉动的杠杆是，你必须要能以更高的比率把线索转化为成交。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I think that is the moment when you start to verticalize, you know, looking at companies that I think have done this moderately well, the Oracles, the Workdays, the SAPs of the world, that's exactly what they've done.
zh: 所以我认为那就是你开始垂直化的时刻，你知道，看看那些我认为在这方面做得还算不错的公司，Oracle、Workday、SAP 这些公司，他们做的正是这件事。

speaker: Unknown
en: One of the reasons I like verticalization in sales teams is what it does to sales cycles.
zh: 我喜欢销售团队垂直化的原因之一，是它对销售周期的影响。

speaker: Unknown
en: Often the messaging is better, it's more accurate, the value props kind of clearer, and I just see a compression in the sales cycle when I see that verticalization.
zh: 通常信息传递更好、更精准，价值主张更清晰，而且每当看到那种垂直化，我都会看到销售周期的压缩。

speaker: Unknown
en: What are the biggest lessons you have on how to compress sales cycles?
zh: 关于如何压缩销售周期，你最大的经验教训是什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: The best way to compress sales cycles is qualifying with more rigor.
zh: 压缩销售周期的最好方法是以更严格的标准做资格筛选。

speaker: Unknown
en: So upstream, you need to understand, does this person have the influence to actually effectuate change?
zh: 所以在上游，你需要弄清楚，这个人是否真的有影响力去促成变革？

speaker: Unknown
en: And are they reasonably committed to doing this within a 12 month period?
zh: 他们是否合理地承诺会在 12 个月内做成这件事？

speaker: Unknown
en: If you could check those boxes, yes, swing at it.
zh: 如果你能勾选那些选项,是的,就放手一试。

speaker: Unknown
en: How do you determine that actually?
zh: 你实际上是怎么判断这一点的？

speaker: Unknown
en: Because a lot of people like to have ego and say they're very important.
zh: 因为很多人喜欢有自尊心，说自己非常重要。

speaker: Unknown
en: And a lot of people will like to please you and say, yes, they'll do it fast.
zh: 而且很多人会想要取悦你，说，是的，他们会很快做到。

speaker: Unknown
en: How do you actually determine it?
zh: 你到底怎么判断呢？

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, you've got to test them.
zh: 是的，你必须测试他们。

speaker: Unknown
en: The way to test them is if they're not in the C-suite or they don't have a VP title, you have to know who their boss is in the org chart.
zh: 这个人会不会——Harry 会不会把 Susan 带进通话？

speaker: Unknown
en: And so if you've had an unbelievable call and you've earned the right to pull in another stakeholder, you have to ask for it.
zh: 所以如果你进行了一场非常棒的通话，并且赢得了引入另一位干系人的权利，你就必须主动要求。

speaker: Unknown
en: And there's a subtle way to do this where it's seemingly a give to get.
zh: 而且有一种很巧妙的方式来做这件事，表面上是一种以给予换取索取。

speaker: Unknown
en: Hey, Harry, today was awesome.
zh: 嘿，Harry,今天太棒了。

speaker: Unknown
en: I have a lot of conviction that we can solve this problem for your business.
zh: 我非常有信心我们能为你的业务解决这个问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: We're gonna knock this demo out of the park.
zh: 我们会把这个 demo 做得极其出色。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm gonna bring on a bunch of my technical resources.
zh: 我会调来一堆我的技术资源。

speaker: Unknown
en: In an effort to bring them onto the call, my ask would be that you bring Susan, your VP of procurement, into this next conversation.
zh: 为了把他们带上通话，我的请求是你把你的采购 VP Susan 带进下一次对话。

speaker: Unknown
en: You'll know right then and there.
zh: 你当场就会知道。

speaker: Unknown
en: Is this person gonna, is Harry gonna bring Susan into the call?
zh: 这个人会不会……Harry 会不会把 Susan 带进通话?

speaker: Unknown
en: Okay, great.
zh: 好的，很好。

speaker: Unknown
en: You may have a champion.
zh: 你可能拥有了一个 champion(内部拥护者)。

speaker: Unknown
en: You may have someone that can infectuate change.
zh: 你可能拥有了一个能够推动变革的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: If not, oh, why aren't you?
zh: 如果没有，哦，为什么不呢？

speaker: Unknown
en: Are you just window shopping?
zh: 你只是随便看看吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Do you not have a relationship with your boss?
zh: 你和你的老板没有关系吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Do you not actually do this?
zh: 你实际上并不做这个吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: So it's a really good way to test that out.
zh: 我觉得一旦你看到这个产品将如何转型和改变你的业务，它给 20 VC 带来的财务影响会远远超过那两美元。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I love that and Susan would love to come.
zh: 所以我很喜欢这个，Susan 也会很乐意来。

speaker: Unknown
en: One thing that's really, it's important for us right now is just cost controls.
zh: 有一件事对我们现在来说真的、真的很重要，那就是成本控制。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so Max, can you help me out here?
zh: 所以 Max,你能帮我个忙吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: You're saying that you're charging four bucks per card or four bucks per seat or four bucks per unit of whatever we're selling.
zh: 你说你收四美元一张卡，或者四美元一个席位，或者四美元一个我们售卖的任何单位。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm going to need it at two.
zh: 我需要二。

speaker: Unknown
en: Are you going to be able to meet me there, Max?
zh: 你能做到吗，Max?

speaker: Unknown
en: I guess to buy some discount.
zh: 我想买点折扣。

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, Harry, we haven't even determined technically if this is going to fit for your organization.
zh: 呃，Harry,我们甚至还没从技术上确定这是否适合你的组织。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so look, we can figure out economics.
zh: 所以你看，我们可以之后再谈经济账。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think once you see how this product is going to transform and change your business, it's going to be a lot more financial impact back to 20 VC than trading two bucks.
zh: 我认为,一旦你看到这个产品将如何转型和改变你的业务,它对 20 VC 带来的财务影响会远大于交易那两块钱。

speaker: Unknown
en: But so you don't engage on discounting because so many founders say to me, I just don't know how to do it.
zh: 但你不参与折扣谈判，因为很多创始人对我说，我只是不知道该怎么做。

speaker: Unknown
en: I want to close the deal, but they want a 20% discount.
zh: 我想成交，但他们想要 20% 的折扣。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, I think early on in the conversation, if we're coming to discuss economics and pricing after call one, that's usually a bad sign.
zh: 是的，我觉得在对话早期，如果我们在第一通电话之后就讨论经济账和定价，那通常是个坏信号。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's not a sophisticated buyer on the other end.
zh: 对面不是一个成熟的买家。

speaker: Unknown
en: Unless it's super down market and you're talking to a 10-person startup founder and you're trying to one-call close, for sure, maybe I'll engage that way and we'll discount to get the deal in the door.
zh: 除非是极度下游市场(down market),你在和一个 10 人的初创公司创始人交谈，并且你想一通电话就成交，那当然，也许我会那样参与，我们会打折把交易拉进门。

speaker: Unknown
en: Upmarket, no, you have to co-author business value assessments.
zh: 在上游市场(upmarket),不，你必须共同撰写业务价值评估。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like you really have to understand what are they trying to solve and what does the total cost of ownership look like?
zh: 就是说你真的必须了解他们想解决什么问题，总拥有成本是什么样的？

speaker: Unknown
en: Are you trying to get a margin win?
zh: 你是想获得毛利率的胜利吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Are you trying to make your accounting function more efficient and give yourself FTE leverage?
zh: 你是想让你的会计职能更高效，给自己带来 FTE(全职员工)杠杆吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: And if you could mutually agree to that, you could circumvent any pricing concessions because hopefully you're driving seven figures in value creation.
zh: 如果你们能就此达成共识，你就可以绕开任何价格让步，因为希望你们正在创造七位数的价值。

speaker: Unknown
en: Speaking of driving seven figures in value creation, we're going to go back to this beautiful interview process because I've impressed you so much.
zh: 说到创造七位数的价值，我们要回到这个精彩的面试流程，因为你已经给我留下了如此深刻的印象。

speaker: Unknown
en: You're so excited for me to join ramp day one and you want to give me a job and it's time for comp design, okay?
zh: 你非常期待我加入 Ramp 的第一天，你想给我一份工作，现在是薪酬设计时间，好吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Compensation design.
zh: 薪酬设计。

speaker: Unknown
en: Can you help me?
zh: 你能帮帮我吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: How do you advise founders on comp design for the first AE and the first SDR?
zh: 你如何为第一个 AE 和第一个 SDR 的薪酬设计给创始人提建议？

speaker: Unknown
en: I usually advise to not have a comp plan.
zh: 我通常建议不要设薪酬方案。

speaker: Unknown
en: I usually advise to do 100% OTE for at least the first two quarters.
zh: 我通常建议至少在前两个季度给 100% OTE(目标总薪酬)。

speaker: Unknown
en: You just don't know what you don't know.
zh: 你只是不知道你所不知道的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I've actually seen founders get into some trouble where they make a quota that gets blown out in the first six months and it's, holy shit, I owe this seller multiple six figures.
zh: 我实际上见过一些创始人因此陷入麻烦，他们定的配额在头六个月就被爆掉了，然后就是，天哪，我欠这个销售好几十万美元。

speaker: Unknown
en: I've seen the inverse happen as well, where you arbitrarily finger in the air, oh, I think this person could close this amount, or I think this person can book this many meetings and it's not attainable.
zh: 我也见过相反的情况，你随意拍脑袋一指，哦，我觉得这个人能成交这个数，或者我觉得这个人能约这么多会议，但结果根本达不到。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then confidence gets hit, and confidence is hard to regain once lost, I find.
zh: 然后信心就受到打击，而我发现，信心一旦失去就很难重新找回。

speaker: Unknown
en: Correct.
zh: 没错。

speaker: Unknown
en: I've seen it though, where even when they do okay, I'm making up numbers.
zh: 不过我也见过这种情况，即使他们做得还行——我随便编个数字。

speaker: Unknown
en: Say they closed 250, but you set me 500.
zh: 你怎么知道他们好不好？

speaker: Unknown
en: 250 would have actually been okay.
zh: 250 其实本来是可以的。

speaker: Unknown
en: It was solid, like decent, not a bad start.
zh: 它是扎实的，还算不错，不算糟糕的开局。

speaker: Unknown
en: But because it was half of what you set, I feel like I'm really bad.
zh: 但因为只有你定的目标的一半，我就觉得自己特别差劲。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's right.
zh: 我们看到他们在各个阶段的推进情况。

speaker: Unknown
en: And in some ways, there's a little bit of benefit to that where, you know, if you get the right person, they've got a fire lit under them and they feel like they're not meeting expectations, there's some healthy angst.
zh: 而且在某种程度上，这有一点好处，就是，你知道吗，如果你招对了人，他们心里会燃起一把火，觉得自己没有达到预期，会有一种健康的焦虑。

speaker: Unknown
en: But it depends on the archetype that you bring in.
zh: 但这取决于你招进来的是哪种类型的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we're 100% OTE.
zh: 所以我们是 100% OTE。

speaker: Unknown
en: When does that change?
zh: 那这个什么时候会变？

speaker: Unknown
en: And how do we then instigate a different discussion around correcting that plan?
zh: 然后我们又该如何围绕修正那个计划开启一场不同的讨论？

speaker: Unknown
en: Data.
zh: 数据。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like typically this would take, it depends on what segments you're going after.
zh: 通常来说，这要取决于你针对的是哪些细分市场。

speaker: Unknown
en: But if you have cycle times that are less than six months, you should have enough data in the system to figure out, okay, this person has been in seat for two months.
zh: 但如果你的成单周期短于六个月，系统里就应该有足够的数据来搞清楚，好，这个人已经入职两个月了。

speaker: Unknown
en: They've ramped for the first 90 days.
zh: 他们度过了前 90 天的爬坡期。

speaker: Unknown
en: We're seeing stage progression here.
zh: 我们正在看到阶段性的进展。

speaker: Unknown
en: We have reason to believe that pipeline is going to be X.
zh: 我们有理由相信管道将会是 X。

speaker: Unknown
en: Let's make a quota that is both
zh: 我们来定一个既

speaker: Unknown
en: Ambitious and somewhat reasonable based on the data that we have.
zh: 有野心、又基于我们手头数据算是比较合理的配额。

speaker: Unknown
en: And you should never hire one seller or one SDR at a time.
zh: 而且你绝对不应该一次只招一个销售或一个 SDR。

speaker: Unknown
en: Because the problem is, how are you going to benchmark their performance?
zh: 因为问题在于，你要如何为他们的表现设定基准？

speaker: Unknown
en: How do you know if they're good?
zh: 你怎么知道他们做得好不好？

speaker: Unknown
en: Are you going to benchmark them against yourself as the founder?
zh: 你要拿他们跟作为创始人的你自己做基准对比吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't think that's reasonable.
zh: 我不认为这合理。

speaker: Unknown
en: Also, as a founder, if you're going to be spending time onboarding a seller, that's laborious, that's expensive, do it in pairs.
zh: 而且，作为创始人，如果你要花时间带一个销售入职，那是费力的、昂贵的，那就成对地招。

speaker: Unknown
en: And there's competition, there's collaboration, they're not lonely.
zh: 这样有竞争，有协作，他们也不孤独。

speaker: Unknown
en: I strongly advise against one at a time.
zh: 我强烈建议不要一次只招一个。

speaker: Unknown
en: Do we always shed one or do we sometimes keep the most?
zh: 那我们总是要裁掉一个吗，还是有时候两个都留？

speaker: Unknown
en: How do you mean?
zh: 你是什么意思？

speaker: Unknown
en: Like if someone isn't performing well?
zh: 比如如果某人表现不佳？

speaker: Unknown
en: By nature of having two, one will always perform worse than the first.
zh: 既然有两个人，按本性来说总有一个会比第一个表现差。

speaker: Unknown
en: How often do you keep them both versus get rid of one?
zh: 你有多大比例是两个都留，而不是裁掉一个？

speaker: Unknown
en: It depends.
zh: 视情况而定。

speaker: Unknown
en: If someone is just complete outlier destroying the other seller,
zh: 如果某人是彻底的离群值，把另一个销售打得毫无还手之力，

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, you probably need to shed that person.
zh: 是的，那你可能就需要裁掉那个人。

speaker: Unknown
en: If it's a 10 to 20% delta, you have to go deeper and unpack it.
zh: 如果差距是 10% 到 20%，你就得深入挖掘一下。

speaker: Unknown
en: Why is this person winning more?
zh: 为什么这个人赢的更多？

speaker: Unknown
en: What structural advantage might they have?
zh: 他们可能有什么结构性优势？

speaker: Unknown
en: Is it pipeline that I gave them?
zh: 是我分配给他们的管道吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Is it pipeline that came from our cap table?
zh: 是来自我们股权结构表的管道吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Is it something else?
zh: 还是别的什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: Do they know the product better?
zh: 他们是不是更懂产品？

speaker: Unknown
en: Are they more motivated?
zh: 他们是不是更有干劲？

speaker: Unknown
en: Do they give a shit and the other person doesn't?
zh: 是不是他们真的在乎而另一个人不在乎？

speaker: Unknown
en: This is on the founder to go ascertain.
zh: 这要由创始人去查明。

speaker: Unknown
en: So for the 100% OT, sorry, going back to that, that's for SDRs.
zh: 那么关于 100% OT，抱歉，回到那个话题，那是针对 SDR 的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Does that change when we're doing comp design for AEs?
zh: 当我们为 AE 做薪酬设计时,这一点会变吗?

speaker: Unknown
en: No, it's unilateral across early go-to-market teams.
zh: 不会,它对早期市场推广团队是单方面统一适用的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Wow.
zh: 哇。

speaker: Unknown
en: What are the big mistakes you think founders make when they're doing comp design?
zh: 你认为创始人在做薪酬设计时会犯哪些大错误?

speaker: Unknown
en: Because again, we have challenging nuances.
zh: 因为再强调一次,我们会遇到有挑战性的细微差别。

speaker: Unknown
en: When you have new products, you want to incentivize them more.
zh: 当你有新产品时,你会想更多地激励他们。

speaker: Unknown
en: You want to encourage bonuses for selling more of those.
zh: 你想鼓励用奖金来推动更多销售。

speaker: Unknown
en: But I don't want to then have a load of people sell all of that and none of the core.
zh: 但我不想然后让一群人把那些全卖光了,核心产品却一个没卖。

speaker: Unknown
en: How do you think about that?
zh: 你是怎么考虑这个问题的?

speaker: Unknown
en: I have so many thoughts on this.
zh: 我对此有非常多的想法。

speaker: Unknown
en: Depends on stage.
zh: 取决于阶段。

speaker: Unknown
en: First, if you're an early stage founder, you're probably still trying to take one product to market and you want to focus on that.
zh: 首先,如果你是一个早期创始人,你可能仍在尝试把一款产品推向市场,并且你想专注于此。

speaker: Unknown
en: You really need to understand your ICP.
zh: 你真的需要理解你的 ICP。

speaker: Unknown
en: Said another way, it's so much more valuable to have
zh: 换句话说,拥有

speaker: Unknown
en: 20 customers that are raving and thrilled about one single product offering than you in a half-ass way serving six customers on multiple products that aren't as thrilled.
zh: 20 个对单一产品服务狂热并感到兴奋的客户,远比你以半吊子的方式服务六个客户、涉及多个产品但他们不那么兴奋要有价值得多。

speaker: Unknown
en: You need to get the tailwind going of case studies, references, and positive momentum across your business.
zh: 你需要让案例研究、推荐和正面势能在整个业务中形成顺风。

speaker: Unknown
en: Later stage though, like where Ramp is today, incentive design is incredibly important.
zh: 不过在后期阶段,比如 Ramp 今天所处的阶段,激励设计是极其重要的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think it's existential to over-incentivize new products to get off the ground.
zh: 而且我认为过度激励新产品以使其起步,是关乎存亡的事。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so thinking through 2X to 3X, quota retirement for new products, you gotta get the, again, you have to get the momentum going such that you earn your way into more multi-product customers, more case studies, more momentum.
zh: 所以要考虑 2 到 3 倍的新产品配额抵扣,你必须——再次强调——你必须让势能滚动起来,这样你才能赢得更多多产品客户、更多案例研究、更多势能。

speaker: Unknown
en: When you get a hire wrong, Max, what do you not see that you should see?
zh: Max,当你招错人时,什么是你没看到但应该看到的?

speaker: Unknown
en: So like for me, sometimes I'm quite overtly aggressive.
zh: 比如对我而言,有时我相当公开地具有攻击性。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's very innate and I'm intense and I'm going to fucking kill competition and I'm going to salivate over it.
zh: 那是非常本能的,我很强势,我要他妈的干掉竞争对手,我会为之垂涎。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I'm happy to talk about that.
zh: 而且我很乐意谈论这一点。

speaker: Unknown
en: The quiet killers, I don't find as easy sometimes to uncover.
zh: 那些安静的「杀手」,我有时不容易发现。

speaker: Unknown
en: That would be the talent that I miss.
zh: 那会是我错过的才能。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I try and correct for that.
zh: 而我努力纠正这一点。

speaker: Unknown
en: When you make a mistake on hiring, what do you miss that you should see?
zh: 当你在招聘上犯错时,什么是你错过了但应该看到的?

speaker: Unknown
en: People in sales, especially leadership, naturally tend to interview well.
zh: 销售人员,尤其是销售领导者,天然倾向于面试表现好。

speaker: Unknown
en: They are sellers by trade.
zh: 他们是以销售为职业的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: They know how to say the right things.
zh: 他们知道怎么说正确的话。

speaker: Unknown
en: They know how to respond extremely quickly in the interview process to show that they are urgent and can follow up ruthlessly.
zh: 他们知道如何在面试流程中极其迅速地回应,以展示他们有紧迫感并且能够毫不留情地跟进。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think the only mistakes that we've made are over-indexing on pedigree and coming from the big name brands and not truly understanding two things.
zh: 我认为我们犯过的唯一错误就是过度看重履历光环和大牌公司的出身,而没有真正理解两件事。

speaker: Unknown
en: One, do they have the agency and do they possess the figure it out X factor where they do not need to be dependent and reliant on so many different internal resources?
zh: 第一,他们是否具备主观能动性,是否拥有那种「自己想办法搞定」的 X 因素,从而不需要依赖和依靠那么多不同的内部资源?

speaker: Unknown
en: And then two, which is related, are they going to go all in?
zh: 然后第二,与此相关,他们会不会全力以赴?

speaker: Unknown
en: Are they going to have a deep obsession?
zh: 他们会不会有一种深度的痴迷?

speaker: Unknown
en: With working at Rant, like it has to become their identity.
zh: 对在 Ramp 工作这件事的痴迷,因为这必须成为他们的身份认同。

speaker: Unknown
en: And if both of those things aren't ascertained crisply in the interview process, it could come out and it's sometimes the wrong hire.
zh: 而如果这两点在面试流程中没有被清晰地确认出来,它就可能浮现出来,而那有时就是错误的招聘。

speaker: Unknown
en: Chad Peters said on the show, legendary sales leader, he said that young people just don't want to work.
zh: Chad Peters 在节目上说过,这位传奇销售领导者说,年轻人就是不想工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that there is a different appreciation for it.
zh: 而且对此有一种不同的看待方式。

speaker: Unknown
en: They want to work from home.
zh: 他们想在家工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: They want work-life balance.
zh: 他们想要工作与生活的平衡。

speaker: Unknown
en: They want mission.
zh: 他们想要使命感。

speaker: Unknown
en: They get burnt out.
zh: 他们会倦怠。

speaker: Unknown
en: They want kombucha.
zh: 他们想要康普茶。

speaker: Unknown
en: Is he right?
zh: 他是对的吗?

speaker: Unknown
en: I love Chad.
zh: 我爱 Chad。

speaker: Unknown
en: He's a beast.
zh: 他是个猛兽。

speaker: Unknown
en: I love Degnan too.
zh: 我也爱 Degnan。

speaker: Unknown
en: That was a fun show.
zh: 那期节目很有趣。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think he's right.
zh: 我认为他是对的。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's a bit provocative, but there are plenty of young professionals that do want to go all in.
zh: 这话有点挑衅，但确实有很多年轻专业人士想要全力以赴。

speaker: Unknown
en: And you have to find them.
zh: 而你必须找到他们。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it's on you to build the culture internally to make sure people want to come into the office every single day.
zh: 而且要在内部打造一种文化，让人们愿意每天来办公室，这是你的责任。

speaker: Unknown
en: We have younger sellers in their career that badge in on Saturdays and Sundays.
zh: 我们有一些处于职业早期的年轻销售，周六周日也打卡上班。

speaker: Unknown
en: Nobody's asking them to do that.
zh: 没人要求他们这么做。

speaker: Unknown
en: But if you create that culture, it's super infectious.
zh: 但如果你打造出那种文化，它极具感染力。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the beauty of that culture is it sniffs out people that do come in that don't want to adhere to that.
zh: 而那种文化的美妙之处在于，它能嗅出那些虽然来了公司、却不想遵守这种文化的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like, look, if you want to work remote, you want to make calls for four hours a day, other ICs in the business are just not going to let that permeate throughout our org.
zh: 就是说，如果你想远程办公，想每天只打四个小时电话，其他 IC 们是不会让这种风气渗透到我们整个组织的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Help me understand.
zh: 帮我理解一下。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm delighted to accept your offer.
zh: 我很乐意接受你的 offer。

speaker: Unknown
en: Thank you so much, Max.
zh: 非常感谢，Max。

speaker: Unknown
en: What have been your biggest lessons on how to onboard new reps effectively?
zh: 在如何有效地给新销售做入职培训方面，你最大的心得是什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: So early stage, you're all locked into a room, okay?
zh: 早期阶段，你们所有人都会被关在一个房间里，好吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: You're going through four very key components.
zh: 你要过四个非常关键的模块。

speaker: Unknown
en: The first of which is the product and the technology that you're selling.
zh: 第一个是你正在销售的产品和技术。

speaker: Unknown
en: The second, the buyer personas that you're selling into.
zh: 第二个是你面向销售的买方画像。

speaker: Unknown
en: The third is the competitive landscape.
zh: 第三个是竞争格局。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the fourth is just like the internal operating chaos of how your systems run and what you need to know as a seller.
zh: 第四个就是你内部运作的混乱，也就是你的系统是怎么跑的，以及作为销售你需要知道什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so on point one in the age of AI, and especially as the next generation of buyers sit and see, they have what I would describe as bullshit repellent.
zh: 在第一点上，在 AI 时代，尤其是当下一代买方坐下来看的时候，他们有我所说的“胡扯 repellent”。

speaker: Unknown
en: They are direct.
zh: 他们很直接。

speaker: Unknown
en: They could get answers quickly.
zh: 他们能很快得到答案。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so the expectation is if they're talking to a seller, they need answers quickly too.
zh: 所以期望就是，如果他们在和销售交谈，他们也需要快速得到答案。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so if you're not technically proficient in your product offering, you're fairly useless as a seller.
zh: 所以如果你对自己的产品在技术上不够精通，那你作为销售基本就是没用的。

speaker: Unknown
en: The second is the buyer personas that you're selling into.
zh: 第二个是你面向销售的买方画像。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is really important.
zh: 这非常重要。

speaker: Unknown
en: You need to know
zh: 你需要知道

speaker: Unknown
en: What their priorities are.
zh: 他们的优先事项是什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: You need to understand their challenges.
zh: 你需要理解他们的挑战。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it differs.
zh: 而且这是有差异的。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you're talking to a CFO of a venture-backed software company, that conversation is gonna be a hell of a lot different than if you're talking to the senior accountant of a construction business.
zh: 如果你和一家风投支持的软件公司的 CFO 交谈，那场对话会和你和一家建筑企业的高级会计师交谈完全不一样。

speaker: Unknown
en: And you need to know the two.
zh: 而且你需要了解这两者。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like one is gonna be super high level.
zh: 比如一个会是超级高层次的。

speaker: Unknown
en: They are trying to drive positive business outcomes.
zh: 他们试图推动积极的业务成果。

speaker: Unknown
en: The accountant might need one workflow that is tied to the month end close that is creating a lot of laborious chaos for them.
zh: 而那个会计师可能只需要一个与月末结账相关的工作流，而那个结账正在给他们制造大量繁琐的混乱。

speaker: Unknown
en: And you need to have that context switching capability.
zh: 你需要具备这种上下文切换能力。

speaker: Unknown
en: The third, the competitive landscape.
zh: 第三个，竞争格局。

speaker: Unknown
en: We obviously play in an incredibly saturated market.
zh: 我们显然处于一个极度饱和的市场。

speaker: Unknown
en: A lot of players claim to do many of the same things.
